title: OIDC discovery against the Keycloak realm's well-known endpoint drives the endpoint record
description: The project reads the realm's discovery document from `<issuerBaseUrl>/realms/<realm>/.well-known/openid-configuration` at boot (or at a cached refresh cadence when the operator prefers a background refresh) and populates the realm record's endpoint fields from it: `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `userinfo_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`, `introspection_endpoint`, `end_session_endpoint`, `issuer`. The record shape the project maintains carries `{ realmSlug, issuerBaseUrl, realmName, clientId, clientSecret (server-only), verificationMode ('jwks' | 'introspection'), roleClaimShape ('client-roles' | 'realm-roles'), scopes[], redirectUri, providerLogout ('redirect' | 'none') }`. A realm whose discovery fetch fails at boot follows the fail-safe posture in REQ-011; a realm whose discovery response omits any endpoint the chosen `verificationMode` depends on is refused at boot with a stable-coded error naming the missing field.
rationale: Keycloak publishes discovery as a matter of course; a project that reads it at boot inherits the realm's current endpoint shape without having to encode a Keycloak URL layout in project code. A realm operator who moves the deployment or reshapes the URL path (a valid Keycloak configuration option through the realm's `hostname-*` settings) does not require a project code change; the discovery pull refreshes the record. Fail-fast on missing endpoints catches an operator who has enabled JWKS-mode against a client whose realm does not publish `jwks_uri` (a rare misconfiguration but a real one).
